The Serra Residences sells 18.8% at launch, with average price of $3,460 psf
article:
Far East Organization has sold 25 of the 133 units at The Serra Residences , or 18.8%, since bookings opened on Oct 16. Transacted prices ranged from $3,123 to $4,200 psf, with an average of $3,460 psf, according to the developer.

The freehold condo on Bassein Road in District 11 is a redevelopment of the former Pastoral View and an adjacent vacant plot. It is a short walk from Novena MRT Station.

The top price was set by the larger of two penthouses, a 2,669 sq ft unit that sold for $11.21 million, or $4,200 psf.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The other units sold comprised nine two-bedroom plus study units, two three-bedroom units, seven four-bedroom units and six four- and five-bedroom premium units.

About 80% of buyers are purchasing for their own use, says Far East Organization in a statement. Singaporeans account for 75% of buyers, and the rest are Singapore permanent residents (PRs) originally from Australia, Britain, China, the Philippines and Taiwan. Buyers include business owners and professionals in the medical, banking and finance, and legal sectors.

“Investors also recognise the long-term rental potential anchored by the expanding HealthCity Novena precinct and the upcoming 2 Moulmein Road lifestyle hub,” the developer adds. The Serra Residences’ connectivity to Orchard Road and the CBD also gives it a broad pool of potential tenants.

The Serra is a single 28-storey tower. Levels four to 16 hold two-bedroom plus study units of 710 to 721 sq ft, three-bedroom units of 764 to 904 sq ft, and four-bedroom units of 958 sq ft.

The Summit , on levels 18 to 28, holds larger four-bedroom units of 1,216 to 1,528 sq ft, five-bedroom premium units of 1,755 sq ft, and the two penthouses of 2,648 and 2,669 sq ft.

title: Thomson Reserve draws 11,800 visitors at preview, highest turnout this year
article:
Thomson Reserve drew 11,800 visitors over its preview weekend of Oct 17–18, the highest turnout this year, ahead of bookings opening on Oct 31.

This surpasses the 10,000 visitors recorded at ParkTown Residence ’s preview last year, said a spokesperson for joint developers UOL Group and CapitaLand Development (CLD).

“It underscores the appeal of a rare five-hectare private residential development offering excellent connectivity, extensive greenery and spacious, upscale homes in the established Upper Thomson neighbourhood,” the spokesperson added.

At 1,268 units, Thomson Reserve is the first project with more than 1,000 units to launch this year.

The spokesperson added that the project’s location, product offering and limited supply nearby have drawn strong interest across unit types from an islandwide pool of buyers. These include first-time homeowners and young families with school-going children, as well as multi-generational families and right-sizers. Younger buyers looking to live near their parents have also shown interest. Ai Tong School is within 1km of the development.

The project is developed by a consortium of CLD, which holds a 50% stake, UOL Group (40%) and UOL’s subsidiary Singapore Land Group (10%). It is a redevelopment of the former Thomson View, which the consortium acquired en bloc in November 2024 for $810 million. The purchase price translated to $1,178 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr), after factoring in land betterment charges and the premium to top up the lease to a fresh 99 years.

The 5ha site, about the size of seven football fields, has a 500m frontage along Upper Thomson Road and is a two-minute walk from Upper Thomson MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

Designed by P&T Consultants, the six residential towers occupy just 12% of the site. The remaining 88% is dedicated to landscaping, water features, and recreational facilities designed by Ecoplan Asia.

More than 45% of residential stacks face the Central Catchment Nature Reserve, and over 80% overlook either greenery or the development’s internal landscaping.

Thomson Reserve has two residential collections. The Classic Collection has 740 units across four 21-storey towers, offering two- to four-bedroom layouts. The Luxury Collection has 528 units in two 30-storey towers, ranging from two-bedroom premium units to five-bedroom suites. Of these, 112 larger four-bedroom premium units and five-bedroom suites have private lift access.

Two-bedroom units make up the bulk of the project, at 716 units or 56.5%. They range from 592 to 775 sq ft, with prices from $1.544 million ($2,608 psf).

There are 350 three-bedroom units (27.6%) of 947 to 1,152 sq ft, priced from $2.503 million ($2,643 psf).

The 174 four-bedroom units (13.7%) range from 1,238 to 1,485 sq ft, with prices from $3.388 million ($2,737 psf).

At the top end are 28 five-bedroom suites of 1,808 sq ft each, making up 2.2% of the development. They occupy a single stack with unblocked views towards MacRitchie Reservoir and the Orchard Road skyline.

ParkTown Residence, the same consortium's 1,193-unit integrated development in Tampines North, sold 1,041 units, or 87%, over its launch weekend in February 2025, at an average of $2,360 psf. It is now 98% sold.

title: Smart Look At The Week Ahead: Meta, Tesla, Netflix And AMEX
article:
More central banks enter the fray with their latest interest-rate decisions ahead of the Fed’s meeting the following week. China will be announcing its loan prime rate. At the September meeting, the People’s Bank of China left its key lending rate unchanged at 3.0% for the 16th straight month. It is expected to leave interest rates where they are again on Tuesday.
Bank Indonesia is expected to keep its key interest rate unchanged at 5.75% thanks to a strengthening of the rupiah. Even though the rate of inflation has increased, it is within the central bank’s target. The Bank of Korea could raise its base rate by 0.25% following a 0.25% increase in September, as the rate of inflation remained above the central bank’s 2% target.
Staying with inflation issues, consumer prices are expected to remain elevated in Canada, the United Kingdom, Japan and Singapore.
On the corporate front
A bunch of tech companies will step into the spotlight in the hope of reigniting market enthusiasm for AI.
Meta
(Nasdaq: META) is expected to report strong third-quarter revenue. But investors will want to know if AI is actually improving advertising revenue by creating new opportunities to generate fresh revenue streams.
Tesla
(Nasdaq: TSLA) is expected to report a drop in both revenue and earnings for the third quarter compared to the previous three months. The car maker has been offering incentives to clear inventory, which could hurt its wafer-thin margins. Investors will also be looking at Tesla’s capital expenditure, which shows no signs of slowing. Free cash flow turned negative in the previous quarter, and the market will want evidence that new product launches will be on track.
Almost every major media company is now promoting stand-alone streaming services that could erode the moat that
Netflix
(Nasdaq: NFLX) has long enjoyed. For the third quarter, revenues are expected to grow thanks to membership gains, pricing and advertising. But margins could narrow as Netflix spends more on creating content.
American Express
(NYSE: AXP) could provide important insights into the spending patterns of its premium customer base, when it reports third-quarter results. The payments processor is expected to post a strong rise in revenue and earnings for the quarter, thanks to an expansion of its product offering and stronger market penetration.
Consumer goods titan
Procter & Gamble
(NYSE: PG) could report modest revenue growth for the first quarter. But earnings could be crimped by rising inflation. The company is facing higher raw material prices, energy costs and transportation expenses.
Other companies that are set to bring home their report cards include industrial conglomerate
3M
(NYSE: MMM), car maker
General Motors
(NYSE: GM), computer giant
IBM
(NYSE: IBM) and healthcare company
Abbott Laboratories
(NYSE: ABT).

title: Smart Reads of the Week: Singapore Bank Stocks, Temasek Share Buybacks, REIT Dividends, and AI Risks
article:
Singapore stocks are finding their footing after last week’s sharp sell-off, when the STI fell 4.1%, led by weakness in bank shares. Meanwhile, concerns over the debt financing the AI boom have unsettled global technology markets.
For investors, these developments raise a familiar question: when share prices fall, are we looking at a buying opportunity or a warning sign?
This week’s Smart Reads explores that question through Singapore’s three major banks. After their recent pullback, we examine whether DBS, OCBC and UOB have become attractive enough to buy, or whether investors should remain patient.
We also look at four Temasek-linked companies aggressively buying back their shares, and three REITs offering yields above 6%. Both may appeal to income investors, but attractive shareholder returns are only meaningful when the underlying businesses can support them.
Elsewhere, the potential deal between StarHub and Keppel involving M1 could reshape Singapore’s telecommunications industry, while the upcoming Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link raises fresh questions for Frasers Centrepoint Trust.
And for long-term investors, we revisit what a S$10,000 investment in iFAST a decade ago would be worth today, alongside a closer look at whether the AI boom’s growing reliance on debt should be a cause for concern.
Here are this week’s top articles:
Top 4 Temasek-Linked Stocks Aggressively Buying Back Their Shares
These Temasek-linked companies are repurchasing their shares, but what do these buybacks really mean for long-term shareholders?
Singapore Bank Shares Have Fallen. Are They Cheap Enough Yet?
DBS, OCBC and UOB have pulled back from their highs. We examine whether their valuations now offer better buying opportunities.
Get Smart: One Lot of DBS For S$14,000?
Smaller SGX board lots make expensive blue chips more accessible, but the real advantage is greater control over your portfolio.
StarHub and Keppel Shares: What the Potential M1 Deal Means for Investors
A potential deal involving M1 could reshape Singapore’s telecommunications industry. We examine what it could mean for both companies.
3 REITs Paying More Than 6%: Are Their Dividends Safe?
Yields above 6% may look tempting, but investors should examine whether the underlying cash flows can sustain those distributions.
The RTS Link Countdown: Is Frasers Centrepoint Trust Built to Withstand the S$290M Retail Drain?
The upcoming RTS Link could shift more spending towards Johor Bahru. Can FCT’s suburban malls withstand the potential impact?
If You Invested S$10,000 in iFAST 10 Years Ago, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today
We look back at iFAST’s decade-long journey to see how patient shareholders have been rewarded.
The AI Boom Is Being Built on Debt: Should Investors Be Worried?
AI investment continues to accelerate, but growing reliance on debt raises important questions about financial sustainability and future returns.
